title: Hexo Redefine 主题博客页脚添加自动更新时间与构建版本记录
content:
背景想在博客的最下方页脚，显示类似 Updated @ 2025-09-12 14:08 · Build a1b2c3d (Toronto, UTC-4) 的信息，每次重新部署时自动更新，不需要手动改。本文记录实现的完整过程和踩坑总结。
效果展示

1. 保证 CNAME 正常保留Hexo 每次生成会清空 public/，所以 CNAME 必须放在 source/ 目录，不能放在根目录。
source/  └── CNAME

这样每次 hexo g 都会自动复制到 public/CNAME，不会丢。

2. 自动生成 build.json在构建前写入一份 source/_data/build.json，保存：

当前时间（多伦多时区）
Git 提交号（短 SHA）
仓库名（GitHub Actions 自动注入）


3. 在页脚插入构建信息因为 Redefine 主题没有调用 Hexo 的 injector()，所以换成 after_render:html 强插：直接在生成好的 HTML 的 <footer> 里插入信息块。
最终脚本放在 根目录的 scripts/build-footer.js：
/* global hexo */const fs = require('fs');const path = require('path');const { execSync } = require('child_process');const BUILD_DIR = path.join(hexo.base_dir, 'source/_data');const BUILD_FILE = path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'build.json');const TZ = 'America/Toronto'; // 多伦多时区// 1) 初始化时写入 build.jsonhexo.extend.filter.register('after_init', function () {  try {    let sha = '';    try {      sha = execSync('git rev-parse --short HEAD', { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] })        .toString().trim();    } catch (_) {}    const ts = Date.now();    const repo = process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY || '';    fs.mkdirSync(BUILD_DIR, { recursive: true });    fs.writeFileSync(BUILD_FILE, JSON.stringify({ ts, sha, repo }, null, 2));    hexo.log.info('[build-meta] wrote %s', path.relative(hexo.base_dir, BUILD_FILE));  } catch (e) {    hexo.log.warn('[build-meta] failed to write build.json: %s', e.message);  }});// 2) 渲染 HTML 后强插页脚hexo.extend.filter.register('after_render:html', function (html, data) {  if (!data || !/\.html?$/i.test(data.path)) return html;  let build = {};  try { build = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(BUILD_FILE, 'utf8')); } catch (_) {}  if (!build.ts) return html;  const when = new Date(build.ts);  const local = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', {    timeZone: TZ, hour12: false,    year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit',    hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit'  }).format(when).replace(',', '');  let tzShort = '';  try {    const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: TZ, timeZoneName: 'shortOffset' })      .formatToParts(when);    tzShort = (parts.find(p => p.type === 'timeZoneName')?.value || '').replace(/^GMT/, 'UTC');  } catch (_) {}  const tzNote = tzShort ? `Toronto, ${tzShort}` : 'Toronto time';  const sha = build.sha || '';  const repo = build.repo || '';  const link = (sha && repo)    ? `<a href="https://github.com/${repo}/commit/${sha}" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="underline decoration-dotted">${sha}</a>`    : (sha ? sha : '');  const snippet =`<div class="build-meta mt-2 text-sm text-third-text-color text-center">  Updated @ ${local}${sha ? ` · Build ${link}` : ''}  <span class="ml-1 text-xs opacity-60">(${tzNote})</span></div>`;  const reInfoContainer = /(<div\s+class="info-container\b[^"]*"[^>]*>[\s\S]*?)(<\/div>\s*<\/footer>)/i;  if (reInfoContainer.test(html)) {    return html.replace(reInfoContainer, `$1${snippet}$2`);  }  if (/<\/footer\s*>/i.test(html)) {    return html.replace(/<\/footer\s*>/i, `${snippet}\n</footer>`);  }  return html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${snippet}\n</body>`);});

效果页脚中会出现一行小字：
Updated @ 2025-09-12 14:08 · Build a1b2c3d (Toronto, UTC-4)


时间已转换为多伦多时区，自动切换夏令时/冬令时  
提交号在 GitHub Actions 上可点击跳转  
时区标注为 text-xs opacity-60，非常低调，不破坏主题的简约风格


4. bookmarks/friends/essays 报错问题Redefine 主题默认会渲染这几个页面，如果 _config.redefine.yml 没配置，会报错：

theme.bookmarks is not iterable
theme.links is not iterable
theme.essays.sort is not a function

解决方案有三种：

不需要这些页面：删除 source/bookmarks|friends|shuoshuo，并在导航里去掉菜单项。  
需要页面但暂时没数据：在 _config.redefine.yml 显式写空数组：bookmarks: []links: []essays: []
保险丝脚本（可选）：redefine-safe-defaults.js，把未定义的字段兜底成 []。它不会覆盖你已有的配置，只在缺失时生效。生产环境配置齐全后，可以删除。


5. 部署与验证
本地构建：
hexo clean && hexo g && hexo dgrep -R "build-meta" public | wc -l   # 检查是否注入成功

GitHub Actions 构建：脚本同样会运行，GITHUB_REPOSITORY 环境变量会让提交号变为可点击链接。检查方式：
curl -s https://<你的域名>/ | grep -c 'build-meta'


总结
CNAME 放 source/ 才能持久。  
scripts/build-footer.js 强插脚本 自动写 build.json 并插入页脚。  
时间转为 多伦多时区，带一个低调的时区标注。  
bookmarks/links/essays 要么删除页面，要么写空数组，要么用 redefine-safe-defaults.js 兜底。  
本地和 Actions 部署都能自动更新，无需手动改动。


这就是一套完整的 Hexo Redefine 页脚自动更新时间 & 构建版本方案 🎉

title: Legendary Python Learning Notes
content:
Hey there!I’m Manda. I’m currently studying Computer Science at the University of Toronto.This is a continuously updated Python learning diary.I will record my error-prone content and notes here. Thank you for coming. Wish you a wonderful day ~
1. Install the environment(1) Install the development environment and compilerYou need to install the development environment and compiler.
Python installation tips:
https://www.python.org/
①. When installing Python, you need to check the “Add Python3.10 to PATH” box below.
②. After completing, click “Disable path length limit” (if it disappears, it is successful)
③. Verify whether Python is installed - Run CMD and enter Python. If Python is prompted and the leading path changes to “>>>”, it is successful.
PyCharm installation tips:
https://www.jetbrains.com/zh-cn/pycharm/download/#section=windows (Select the gray free personal version)
①. Check the first and bottom two checkboxes in the installation options. The contents are Create Desktop ShotCut (creating a desktop shortcut) and Create Associations (.py) (to compile all .py files using PyCharm).
②. DATASHARNG is optional.
③. If you want to use Chinese, search for “Chinese” in the Plugins section and install the plugin with the “汉” icon. Restart PyCharm following the prompts.
(2). PyCharm configuration
When creating a new project, remember to select the installed Python version (3.10) in the “Basic Editor”

Do not check Create main.py Welcome

Do not touch the venv in the project folder. This is the project’s independent Python virtual environment. Do not change or write to it!

When creating a new file, click Cancel when prompted to “Add file to Git” (you can check “Do not prompt again”)

To open the editing panel, right-click the project folder in PyCharm and select New-Python File (note that you should not create it in venv)


2. Basic knowledge(1). Data types


数据类型
示例1
示例2



字符串 str
"Hello"
"呐!"


整数 int
6
-32


浮点数 float
6.0
10.07


布尔类型 bool
True
False


空值类型 NoneType
-
-


NoneType 就叫 None
②.字符串 strA string of characters representing text (can be enclosed in single or double quotes!)
The len function returns the length of the string!
By the way, spaces, numbers, and symbols all take up a single length.
However, a complete transition character takes up a single length. For example, len(‘\n’) = 1, len(‘hi!!\n’) = 5.
# Get the string lengthlen('Hello')len('Yo!')

After adding the print event the output is as follows
52

Next we will learn a new thing: index
[buy] index, use English parentheses, for example [[]][/buy]
You can extract a single character at a certain position in the string!
"Hello"[3]

Note! The index order starts from 0, which means from left to right it is 0, 1, 2, 3…
For example, the code above returns the fourth letter (although it is written as 3), which means “l”
③. Integer/Floating Point Number int/floatFloating point numbers are called float in Python and support mathematical operations.
④. Boolean Type boolCan only return true or false (1 or 0) True or False (note that T and F are capitalized!!!)
Often used in logical reasoning
⑤. Null Type NoneTypeThis type has only one value: None.
None ≠ 0 or “ “ or False; it represents the absence of a value.
If you need a variable but don’t know its value yet, you can use NoneType as a placeholder.
# e.g.my_wife = None


When you’re unsure of an object’s type, you can use ↓
[buy]Type function: Returns the object’s type[/buy]
Homework ↓

lesson 12 Download

(2). Python interactive mode①. Command line modeWrite the command → Save → Run
This is our most normal way of writing code
②. Interactive modeYou can think of it as green run mode
You can run it in the console under cmd/Pycharm
The first advantage is that you don’t need to create any files and can run it directly
And you don’t need to write print statements, Python will directly output the results of the operation
(3). VariablesBasic syntax: variable name = variable value
e.g.
my_love = "15199999999"

 As mentioned earlier, Python runs line by line from top to bottom. If you print first and then assign a value, the program will not get the result. 
my_love = "15199999999"print("Call: " + my_love)

In this code, my_love is not enclosed in quotes, so it appears as a variable.
If you want to store multiple variables, you can use another variable to store them.
For example, use my_friend to store the original my_love and then overwrite the new value of my_love.
my_love = "15199999999" # The original value of the mylove variablemy_friend = my_love # Assign mylove to the new variablemy_love = "13366666666" # Assign the new value to mylove

Hard rules for Python variable names: They can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores, cannot start with a number, and cannot contain keywords.   Python variable names are case-sensitive! userage and userAge are two different variables! 
Note that the reason I mentioned that they cannot be keywords is because if you assign a value to print…
print = "u123"

Then you won’t be able to use print to print later!
print = "u123"print("Hello")

Because in the current program, print is no longer a function with printing function
In PyCharm, if the variable name you type turns into color, it means it is keyword 2. It is recommended to change it!
(4). Python mathematical operationsFirst, Python uses an asterisk [*] for multiplication and a slash [/] for division
Second, Python also operates according to the priority of mathematical operations
Parenthesis are calculated first, followed by exponentiation, then multiplication and division, and finally addition and subtraction
In Python, exponentiation can be represented by two asterisks connecting numbers. For example, the square is [** 2]
Or you can import a math function library and add import math at the beginning
import math

Then you need to add math at the beginning of the function name when calling it below
import mathmath.functionname(...)// For example, calculate sin1 Then use the sin function with a value of 1.math.sin(1)// This step only performs the calculation but does not print the result. So to get the result, you can write it like this↓print(math.sin(1))// Or assign the value print to a variableresult = math.sin(1) // Register a function named result to store the result of the mathematical operationprint(result) // Print the value of result// P.S. The code editor for this part has an error and recognizes it as a Lua script// You can only write comments in Lua, but Python's comment method is the pound sign (Shift + 4)

For more mathematical functions and usage methods, you can click the link below to jump to the official documentation
https://docs.python.org/zh-cn/3/library/math.html

Example ①
❤Goal: Calculate the two roots of a quadratic function
❤【-x²-2x+3=0】
Use the root-finding formula

❤【-x²-2x+3=0】
In this formula, a = -1, b = -2, c = 3
a = -1b = 2c = 3# First, assign variables# Because the root-finding formula involves addition or subtraction, there are two results, so we need to write two code snippets~# First, calculate the addition solution-b + (b ** 2 - 4 * a * c) **(1/2)# b² - 4ac, the square root is replaced with the square root of one-half!# If you've imported the math library, you can use the sqrt function, which returns the square root.

import math # First import the librarya = -1b = 2c = 3(-b + math.sqrt(b ** 2 - 4 * a * c)) / 2 * a# This is the first solution we're looking for# For the second solution, simply change the sign to a negative.(-b - math.sqrt(b ** 2 - 4 * a * c)) / 2 * a# Remember to use print(), otherwise the result won't be output!

If you want to calculate other functions, this is even more convenient; just change the values ​​of a, b, and c.
Tip: If you want to make the code simpler, you can register a value called delta (△).
Specify it as b² - 4ac
a = 1b = 9c = 20delta = b ** 2 - 4 * a * cprint((-b + math.sqrt(delta)) / (2 * a))print((-b - math.sqrt(delta)) / (2 * a))
This makes it much more convenient.
pythonProject
Oh, and there’s a str function in lines 6 and 7 in this image.
If you don’t add it, you’ll get a message like
can only concatenate str (not “float”) to str
I searched online and found that

In Python, the print function doesn’t recognize two data types simultaneously. In the code, money is of type float and preceded by a string. It can be printed by itself using print(money). However, since it has a string at the beginning, the money at the end also needs to be a string. To do this, simply convert the type: print(“Total price is “ + str(money))
https://blog.csdn.net/fqfq123456/article/details/119506330

So, I converted the variables resulta and resultb to strings.
This is additional information I learned while debugging and is not part of the main storyline of this diary!

(5). Comments
When you first write code, only you and God know what it does. After a few days, only God knows.


The Importance of Comments

Comments in Python use the pound sign [#]
For example
# This is a line of comment

 In the Win+PyCharm environment, click CTRL+? You can annotate the selected content with one click (same as VSCODE)
Tip: You can also use triple quotes “”” to wrap the comment
"""This is amulti-linecomment""


(6). Data structure①. ListIn Python, to represent a list (data structure), use a pair of square brackets[ ]
# e.g.shopping_list = []

If you want to preset data, you can use quotes to enclose it and use English commas to separate it
# listshopping_list = ["keyboard","mouse"]

Here, the course progress introduces a new method append. Other methods can be found under the heading 4. Method!
[buy] method: Similar to a function, but methods are generally called as [object.method name(…)]. Functions are Use [Function Name (Object)] like this. [/buy]
# Method: (For details on methods, see 4. Methods below.)shopping_list = ["Keyboard","Mouse"]shopping_list.append("Display")# This code adds a new item, "Display," to the shopping_list list.

Another point is that lists can be used like strings to find the number of elements using the len function!
For example
# len function to find the number of elements in a listlist1 = ["A","B","C"]print(len(list1))

Running this will print 3, indicating that the list contains 3 items.
Of course, you can use indexing to access the element at a specific position in a list!
For example
# retrieval of an element at a specific position in a listlist1 = ["Position 1","Position 2","Position 3"]print(list1[0])

It should be noted that the index is from left to right, with the first position set to 0 and increasing in sequence.
The position of the last data = the length of the list - 1
The output is:
Position 1

6.1.1. List index assignmentIf there is a list with elements keyboard, monitor, and hard disk. And you want to change the element at the monitor position to a new element.
You can write it like this↓
# index overwrite element (position)shopping_list = ["mouse","keyboard","monitor"]shopping_list[1] = "sound" # Change the index position to 1, that is, the element at the "keyboard" position is overwritten with "sound"print(shopping_list)


②. DictionaryDictionary is used to store key-value pairs, Keys have corresponding values, and keys are used to look up values.
To represent an empty dictionary: Use a pair of curly braces [{ }]
# Dictionary - Key-Value Pairscontacts = {"Xiaoming" : "13700000000","Xiaohua" : "13700000001"}

 Note: Use a colon to assign a value to a key, for example, assign “Xiaoming” : “13700000000”. Multiple key-value pairs are separated by commas. 
To get the value of a key, use the dictionary name followed by square brackets with the key inside.
For example
# Get the value of a key in a dictionarycontacts = {"Xiaoming" : "13700000000","Xiaohua" : "13700000001"}contact["Xiaoming"]

 Note: The key type must be immutable! ! For example, a mutable data type like “list” cannot be used as a key.
6.2.1. TuplesA data structure that looks very similar to lists, but is immutable. This is the tuple.
# Tuples

It looks very similar to lists, but there are differences.
What’s visible to the naked eye is
# Tuple vs. Listexample_tuple = ("mouse", "keyboard", "keycap") # This is a tupleexample_list = ["mouse", "keyboard", "keycap"] # This is a list

Note that since tuples are immutable, methods like remove and append are not available.

Although it’s not very flexible or convenient, it can help us achieve our goal of storing three Zhang Weis in our address book.
# Where did the three Zhang Weis come from? ?contacts = {("张伟",23):"13800000001",("张伟",34):"13700000002",("张伟",56):"13600000003",}

At this point, these tuples are the keys of the dictionary. When looking for a phone number, you can use the entire tuple as the key.
For example
# Based on the above codezhangwei23_phone = contacts[("张伟",23)]# Get the Zhang Wei whose phone number is 23print(zhangwei23_phone)

Running print will return the phone number of Zhang Wei whose phone number is 23: 13800000001

6.2.2 Editing Dictionary Content1. Adding KeysFirst, dictionaries, like lists, are mutable; key-value pairs can be added or deleted.
If you want to add a new key-value pair to a dictionary, you can write it like this:
dictionary name [key] = value
For example
# Add a new key-value pair to the dictionarycontacts = {"Xiaoming":"13800000022","Zhangwei":"13700000002","Xiaohua":"13700000095",}# dictionary name [key] = valuecontacts["美女A"] = "15500000001"

However, this approach has a drawback: if the key-value pair already exists, the value corresponding to the key will be overwritten.
What should we do?
We need to know if the key already exists in the dictionary.
In this case, we can use [key in dictionary]
It will return a Boolean value.
# key in dictionarycontacts = {"Xiao Ming":"13800000022","Zhang Wei":"13700000002","Xiao Hua":"13700000095",}print("Xiao Ming" in contacts)# This `in` function returns a Boolean value.

2. Deleting a KeyIf you want to delete a key-value pair, you can use del.
del dictionary name[key]
This will delete the key and its corresponding value from the dictionary.
Note, however, that if the key doesn’t exist, Python will report an error.
# del Delete a keycontacts = {"Xiaoming":"13800000022","Zhangwei":"13700000002","Xiaohua":"13700000095",}del contacts["Xiaoming"] # Delete the key "Xiaoming" from the dictionaryprint(contacts)

3. Number of Dictionary ContentsThe old friend len can also be used to output the number of key-value pairs in a dictionary.
# len Output the number of key-value pairs in a dictionary.contacts = {"Xiaoming":"13800000022","Zhangwei":"13700000002","Xiaohua":"13700000095",}print(len(contacts))

Practical Section: Input & If & Dictionary Combining Popular Speech Meaning Dictionary
Goal: Look up a popular phrase in the dictionary and return its meaning. If it doesn’t exist, return “not found.”

(7). For loop iterationThe iterative object can be a list, dictionary, string, etc.~
Iteration means doing something to the data in the list (dictionary) in order
The basic structure of Python’s For loop looks like this↓

For example, to find the body temperature that meets specific requirements in the body temperature list, you can write it like this↓
# For example, let's search for temperatures that meet specific requirements in a temperature list.temperature_list = [36.4, 36.6, 36.2, 37.0] # This is a predefined temperature list.for temperature in temperature_list # Search from t_listif temperature >= 38:print(temperature)print("Abnormal temperature! Game over! QAQ")

You can simply check the number of games over to determine how many people have a fever.
However, this method doesn’t tell you which person has a fever.
So, we need to create a dictionary with employee ID (or name) as the key and temperature as the value.
Using a for loop, we can filter out people with a fever.
Python dictionaries have three methods.

First, dictionary_name.keys returns all the keys in the dictionary (where “111” is located).
dictionary_name.values will return all values ​​in the dictionary (that’s where “36.4” is).
dictionary_name.items will return all key-value pairs in the dictionary.
We can use a for loop with an if statement to print the keys corresponding to values ​​with a temperature greater than 38 degrees Celsius!
This will print the employee ID of the person with a fever!
# for + if + t_dict.items prints the employee ID of the person with a fevertemperature_dict = {"111":36.4,"112":36.6,"113":37.0,"114":38.1,"115":35.1}for stuff_id,temperature in temperature_dict.items():if temperature >= 38:print(stuff_id)

Note: Two variables (stuff_id and temperature) are used after the for loop because dictionary_name.items() is assigned a tuple consisting of a key and a value during the for loop. This is equivalent to assigning the first element of the tuple to staff_id and the second element to temperature.
To put it simply, there are two values ​​in the for statement: the employee ID and the temperature. Because they exist in pairs in the dictionary,
therefore, the for statement must correspond!
This is equivalent to the following:
#temperature_dict = {"111":36.4,"112":36.6,"113":37.0,"114":38.1,"115":35.1}for temperature_tuple in temperature_dict.items():staff_id = temperature_tuple[0]temperature = temperature_tuple[1]if temperature >= 38:print(staff_id)

(7.1).range - A magical combination with forDo you know how Gauss calculated the sum from 1 to 100?
The famous Gauss formula: (first term + last term) x number of terms / 2
range is used to represent a sequence of integers.
The first value in the brackets represents the starting value, and the second value represents the ending value.
For example, range(5,10) yields 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, in that order.
Note! The ending value is not included!
# e.g.for i in range(5,10)print(i)

This code means assigning values ​​of 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 to i and printing them in sequence
In addition, range can contain a third parameter
The third number (2) in range(5,10,2) represents the step size, that is, the number of numbers to step over each time
If you want to print all odd numbers between 1 and 9
# Print all odd numbers between 1 and 9for num in range(1,10,2)print(num)

Then we can solve Gauss’s problem like this:
# 1+2+...+99+100 = ?total = 0 # Define a new variable called total, initially 0for i in range(1,101): # range lets the variable i be 1, 2, 3... until 100total = total + i # Add i to the total variable in increments of 1 Variableprint(total) # Print total variable

 Backslash + n [\n] indicates a line break

This section discusses nested conditional statements (adding another conditional statement within a conditional statement).
# Nested Conditional Statements (Remember to indent correctly!)if [Condition 1]:if [Condition 2]:[Statement A]else:[Statement B]

Note! Statement A is nested within both Condition 1 and Condition 2. Both must be met!
The same applies to adding an else clause. Both conditions must be met before the statement is triggered.
 Python typically uses 4 spaces for indentation. Statements below the if or else clause will be indented to determine which branch they belong to. 
Of course, we can also add an else clause to condition 1.
This means that if condition 1 isn’t met, condition 2 won’t be considered, let alone triggering A or B.
Only condition C will be triggered. ↓
# Nested conditional statements (remember to indent correctly!)if [condition 1]:if [condition 2]:[Statement A]else:[Statement B]else:[Statement C]

**Introduction: There’s also a thing called elif! **It can also be used for nested conditionals.
# elifif [condition 1]:[Statement A]elif [condition 2]:[Statement B]elif [condition 3]:[Statement C]else:[Statement D]

This structure is simpler and clearer.
However, since Python executes from top to bottom, if both conditions 2 and 3 are met, Python will only execute statement B (condition 2).
Because condition 2 is at the top, once that branch is entered, other conditions at the same level will not be considered!
